question: What does the Canada National Parks Act say should come first when the minister manages a national park?

Preamble

WHEREAS Canada is a country that enjoys a pristine natural environment and recognizes that the conservation of ecosystems is fundamental to the well-being of Canada;

WHEREAS the Government of Canada desires, in cooperation with other governments, local authorities and aboriginal people, to protect and conserve the parks of Canada for present and future generations;

AND WHEREAS the Government of Canada has established national parks in order to protect representative examples of each of the natural regions of Canada and to present them to Canadians and the world for their appreciation and enjoyment;

NOW, THEREFORE, Her Majesty, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate and House of Commons of Canada, enacts as follows:

Short title

1. This Act may be cited as the Canada National Parks Act. Definitions

2. The definitions in this section apply in this Act. “Canada’s national parks system” « réseau des parcs nationaux du Canada »

“Canada’s national parks system” means the system of national parks in Canada established under this Act. “Convention” « Convention »

“Convention” means the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, signed at Paris on November 23, 1972. “federal property” « propriété fédérale »

“federal property” means any lands, waters and natural resources under the administration, management and control of the Minister. “historic place” « lieu historique »

“historic place” means any site, building or other place that is designated under section 32 or 33. “Minister” « ministre »

“Minister” means such member of the Queen’s Privy Council for Canada as is designated by the Governor in Council as the Minister for the purposes of this Act. “national historic site” « lieu historique national »

“national historic site” means any site, building or other place that is designated under section 32 or 33. “national park” « parc national »

“national park” means a park that is established under subsection 5(1) and that is listed in Schedule 1. “park reserve” « réserve de parc »

“park reserve” means a park reserve that is established under subsection 5(2) and that is listed in Schedule 2. “property” « bien »

“property” means any real, personal, movable or immovable property. “superintendent” « directeur »

“superintendent” means a person appointed under the Parks Canada Agency Act who holds the office of superintendent of a park or of a national historic site. “World Heritage Committee” « Comité du patrimoine mondial »

“World Heritage Committee” means the committee established under Article 23 of the Convention. World Heritage Convention

3. The Convention is approved, accepted and ratified and the Stone of Destiny (Coronation Stone) is recognized and declared to be cultural property of outstanding interest to humanity. Canada National Parks Act

Establishment of National Parks

Establishment of national parks

5. ( 1) There is hereby established a national park in Canada for each of the areas of land or water referred to in Schedule 1. Establishment of park reserves

(2) There is hereby established a park reserve in Canada for each of the areas of land or water referred to in Schedule 2. Aboriginal land, rights or interests

6. For greater certainty, nothing in this Act affects any existing aboriginal or treaty rights of the aboriginal peoples of Canada that are recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982. Powers, Duties and Functions of the Minister

Minister’s powers, duties and functions

7. The Minister is responsible for the implementation of this Act and has superintendence of the parks and of historic places. Management plans

8. ( 1) The Minister shall, within one year after the establishment of a park, and within five years after the amendment of this Act by section 16, if the Minister considers the amendment to be significant, as soon as feasible, prepare a management plan for the park that

(a) is based on a resource and spatial analysis of the park;

(b) provides for the implementation of the vision, purpose, principles of management and key strategies for the protection and presentation of the park;

(c) specifies the main measures that are to be taken for the implementation of the vision, purpose, principles of management and key strategies for the protection and presentation of the park; and

(d) identifies the resource requirements and evaluation mechanisms required for the implementation of the main measures. Consultation

(2) The Minister shall offer to consult with the council of the first nation, if any, on whose reserve lands the park is situated or with any first nation that has traditional ties to the park when preparing the management plan. Amendment

(3) The Minister may at any time amend the management plan. Minister to consult
